waypoints.name: Rainy Pass PCT Trailhead
waypoints.note: PCT north trailhead off Highway 20 at Rainy Pass.

waypoints.name: Molar Tooth
waypoints.note: Follow the PCT ~1.5 mi to near Porcupine Creek, then ascend the ridge NE to the peak between Cutthroat Pass and Cutthroat Peak.

_raw.permit_type: Free self-issue day-use wilderness permit (May 15 - Oct 31)
_raw.special_requirements: No overnight camping within 0.25 miles of Cutthroat Lake. No tents allowed above Cutthroat Pass due to fragile wildflower meadows. Class 4 scrambling route; rappel gear required for descent.
_raw.parking_pass_required: Northwest Forest Pass ($5 day pass or $30 annual) or pay $5 cash at trailhead
_raw.seasonal_closure_dates: Access typically May 15 - Oct 31; snow may close access earlier/later

access.fees: None beyond the parking or entrance fee this route already lists.
access.rules: No climbing or wilderness permit required for day climbing. Dispersed camping capped at 10 days; no camping within ¼ mile of Cutthroat Lake; no campfires at dispersed sites; bear-resistant food storage required; dogs on leash ≤6 ft.
access.permit: Free self-issue day-use wilderness permit (May 15 - Oct 31)
access.closures: Access typically May 15 - Oct 31; snow may close access earlier/later
access.seasonal: WA-20 (North Cascades Highway) closes gate-to-gate roughly early December–mid/late April; the entire Washington Pass corridor is car-inaccessible in winter.
access.land_manager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
access.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
access.passRequired: Northwest Forest Pass ($5 day pass or $30 annual) or pay $5 cash at trailhead

overnight_permit.where: General Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest land; a day-use fee or Northwest Forest Pass covers parking. No camping is allowed within a quarter mile of Cutthroat Lake.
